Matt worked on **JP Morgan Chase**’s ACCESS Next Generation payments platform from **August 2009 to June 2012**, serving as Technology Delivery Lead and Senior Technology Architecture Manager. The bank was consolidating regional treasury systems into a single global portal, but Bottomline Technologies’ WebSeries platform did not provide all the payment modules, security controls, or workflows its corporate clients required. Each payment type had distinct formatting, validation, compliance, and approval requirements.

Matt managed a blended team of **40+** **Accenture** and bank resources across Mumbai, Bangalore, and the US. He spent **70 to 80%** of his time embedded at Bottomline’s Portsmouth offices, working through where the platform’s native capabilities ended and bespoke engineering was required.

He designed and delivered ACH, wire, FX/cross-border, and tax payment modules. These included NACHA file validation, integration with the bank’s foreign exchange engine, and Message Authentication Code security so corporate users could verify payment integrity before release. He also built contextual help into payment screens, explaining wire fields, tax codes, and FX parameters within the workflow.

Alongside the payment engine, Matt designed the centralized gateway for message transformation, protocol translation, and routing across **12 countries**, replacing fragmented point-to-point integrations. He introduced bulk entitlement changes across users, accounts, and products from a single screen, replacing individual permission configuration and reducing administration from days to minutes.

For migration and rollout, he coordinated legacy-data verification, preserved compliance traceability, and mapped jurisdiction-specific requirements into data visibility and access controls. Regional launches were sequenced by regulatory readiness rather than a single global deployment.

ACCESS launched in **April 2011**, serving **135,000+** corporate, financial institution, government, and municipal clients across **180+ countries**. The legacy migration completed without disruption to live payments, and the regional compliance framework enabled rollout across APAC, EMEA, and the Americas without regulatory blockers.

Matt leads with empathy, clarity, and purpose. He describes the teams he inherited as “over-processed, under-trusted, waiting for permission instead of owning outcomes.” His focus is on removing those barriers: making intent explicit, creating psychological safety so people can speak honestly, and pushing decisions to the people closest to the work.

At **Accenture’s** Cloud Innovation Center, that included establishing a “permit to fail” learning environment. Teams had avoided risks because they feared blame. Matt organized non-punitive post-mortems, emphasized lessons rather than pointing fingers, and supported lean, low-stakes experiments. Teams began experimenting more freely, applied post-mortem learnings to subsequent sprints, and prevented recurrence of identified failure patterns.

He also builds balanced teams: Product + Engineering + Design together. Rather than keeping those roles in separate silos, Matt assembled engineers, product managers, and UX architects with equal participation and shared accountability. He embedded pair programming, collaborative coding, retrospectives, and knowledge-sharing sessions. Teams could voice feedback and implement changes autonomously instead of waiting for permission.

His coaching focus is to help teams think clearly, not just execute tasks. He pairs that with automation, continuous delivery, and quality-first practices. At the Cloud Innovation Center, teams accelerated delivery **4x** after embracing lean product and modern engineering practices. In the balanced-team work, teams reduced handoffs and project delays, improved satisfaction and retention, and achieved **zero-defect production code**.

Matt’s work centers on Execution & Delivery, Org & Working-Model Transformation, and Talent & Enablement: building products and platforms, changing how teams work, and building the organization that delivers them. His career spans engineer to Director, including banking modernization at **JP Morgan Chase**, **RBC**, **Capital One**, and **HSBC**, recovering troubled programs, and architecting cloud-native systems from prototype to production.

At **Accenture**, clients needed to move beyond waterfall delivery, feature factories, and siloed teams. Matt built the Atlanta and Tampa Cloud Innovation Centers from **0 to 150+ practitioners**, with full P&L accountability. He brought product managers, designers, and engineers together in balanced teams, embedded pair programming, test-driven development, and automated pipelines, and adapted those practices for legacy systems, compliance, and enterprise governance. Rather than presenting methodology slides, he invited prospective clients to observe standups and teams solving problems together.

He also built the talent pipeline: tailored training, experienced mentors paired with junior hires, and an “I do, we do, you do” learning model. Practitioners progressed from guided to independent delivery. The talent program achieved near-zero attrition in its first **2 years**.

At **Capital One**, slow iterations and misaligned priorities were extending time-to-market. Matt introduced a client-prioritized, testable backlog and disciplined red-green-refactor practice within an **8-person** team. They delivered features **3 to 4x faster** than other **Accenture** teams on the same engagement, with **zero production defects**. The client sought to retain the team beyond its planned end.

Across the Cloud Innovation Centers, the work reached **30+ product engagements** and **15+ Fortune 500 clients**, achieving **4X faster velocity** and **zero-defect deployments**. Delivery excellence and customer relationships drove **\$100M+ in repeat business**, with client teams continuing the practices after engagements ended.

🐾 Here’s how Matt built AWS Launchpad.

At **Accenture’s** Liquid Studio, traditional training programs couldn’t keep pace with rapidly evolving AWS technologies. Engineers had gaps in cloud competency, and cloud adoption was slowing. The Atlanta Innovation Hub needed a structured enablement program that would help engineers earn certifications and prepare them to lead cloud-native initiatives, rather than rely on theory alone.

From **July 2018** to **November 2019**, Matt led AWS Launchpad in collaboration with AWS. He designed structured learning paths and certification programs covering AWS core services, including Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB, Kubernetes, and ECS/Fargate, alongside cloud-native application development.

The program paired those learning paths with interactive workshops and hands-on labs. Engineers worked in real-world AWS environments to reinforce practical application over theory. Certification preparation was part of the program, but so was applying the services engineers would use on cloud transformation projects.

Matt also established cloud expert mentorship teams to embed best practices and retain institutional knowledge. He organized group coaching sessions and knowledge-sharing workshops, giving participants support beyond the formal training. The combination was structured learning, practical work, and mentor-based training, rather than a stand-alone course.

More than **200 professionals** earned AWS certifications, including AWS Solutions Architect and DevOps Engineer certifications. The program accelerated cloud adoption and the launch of cloud-native initiatives at **Accenture**, with mentorship and knowledge-sharing supporting continued learning across teams.
